title: Quantum tunneling leakage in atomic-scale gates
bottleneck: At gate lengths of a few nanometers, electrons tunnel directly through barriers regardless of transistor state, producing leakage currents that waste power and heat chips even when idle. Gate dielectrics are already a few atoms thick; thinning them further barely helps while new channel materials are immature. This physics floor ends Dennard scaling: smaller transistors no longer automatically mean proportionally lower power.
why_it_blocks: Leakage caps the usable transistor count per chip and per watt, directly limiting AI accelerator throughput and battery-powered compute. Every future node must now buy efficiency from architecture and materials rather than from shrinking, raising design cost and complexity.
current_state: High-k dielectrics, GAA electrostatics, and backside power delivery mitigate but do not eliminate tunneling. Research into 2D-material channels and negative-capacitance FETs aims to beat the 60 mV/decade limit, with no production deployment yet.
